name: Andal
credit: Traditional painting of Andal · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Andal (also called Kodai), the only woman among the twelve Alvars, the Tamil poet-saints devoted to Vishnu, belongs to the ninth century. Tradition places her at Srivilliputtur, where she was found as a child by the temple priest Periyalvar and brought up as his daughter, and says that she gave her whole love to Krishna and was at last received into the shrine of Ranganatha at Srirangam.

Two poems of hers survive, both in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham: the Nachiyar Tirumoli, in which she longs for the god as a bride, and the thirty-stanza Tiruppavai, in which she speaks as a cowherd girl rousing her friends for the dawn bath of the month of Margali. The Tiruppavai is sung daily in Vaishnava worship through that month, and is among the works prescribed for Tamil study.
